newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Long-dated Russian T-bill prices fall up to 0.3.
newsitem.headline: Long-dated Russian T-bill prices fall up to 0.3.

text.p: Prices of long-dated Treasury bills fell in active trading on Monday, but demand quickly reappeared as yields backed up, dealers said.
Prices fell by up to 0.3 points in the first 15 minutes of trading, with less than one trillion roubles in the trading system, indicating low demand after last week's fall in yields to record lows.

"After prices fell at the start of trading, yields on these issues rose to 20.5 percent from 19.0 which stimulated buying, as a result of which they're now back at Friday's levels," said Bank MFK dealer Andrei Koshchy.

But dealers said the low amount of funds in the system -- banks deposited only 728 billion roubles in their trading accounts before the market opened -- meant there was little potential for prices to rise, and prices could drift off by the end of trading.

Despite the low amount of funds in the system, with banks transferring only 728 billion roubles before trade started, turnover was high, reflected in heavy use of the Central Bank's two-day repo facility.

Rates on the facility were cut from Monday to 18 percent from 20 percent on loans taken out on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday, and to 21 from 25 percent for loans taken out on Thursday and Friday. The repo facility gives designated authorised dealers an overdraft in the T-bill market.
The cut in repo rates coincides with a reduction in the Central Bank's refinancing rate announced last week, to 24 percent as of Monday from 36 percent, following the recent sharp drop in yields.
The refinancing rate, not used for any particular lending facility, is effectively a ceiling on T-bill yields.
The central bank also cut rates on its Lombard lending facilities.
"With money market rates staying so high, it's profitable to buy using the repo," Koshchy said.
Overnight money rates rose to 20/25 percent from 12/17, while the rouble firmed to 5,756/69 per dollar for today delivery from Friday's 5,760/62 for tomorrow delivery.

Dealers said prices of long-dated issues after the initial drop were up to 0.1-0.2 lower than on Friday, while short and medium dates were inactive, except for the series 21074 three-month bills auctioned last Wednesday.
At 0800 GMT taxable T-bills were yielding 20 percent, and tax-free issues were at 17-19 percent.
